::: {#rem-diagonalization}
#### The diagonal argument

Picture an infinite table with one row for each binary string $w$,
one column for each binary string $x$,
and the entry in row $w$ and column $x$ equal to $M_w(x)$,
or to a mark for "runs forever".
Each row lists everything one machine does.
UC is built from the diagonal entries $M_w(w)$,
and it disagrees with row $w$ in column $w$ for every $w$,
so no row [decides](models-of-computation.qmd#def-tm-computes) it.
@arora2009computational [chapter 3] use the same idea to prove the hierarchy theorems.

:::
